Thought: There seems to be an issue with using the calculation tool. I will manually calculate the moles of EDTA used. The volume of EDTA solution needs to be converted from cm³ to dm³ before calculating the moles.

1. Convert the volume of EDTA from cm³ to dm³.
2. Calculate the moles of EDTA using the concentration and the converted volume.

Let's proceed with this calculation step by step.

1. Convert 21.70 cm³ to dm³:
   \[
   \text{Volume in dm}^3 = \frac{21.70 \, \text{cm}^3}{1000} = 0.02170 \, \text{dm}^3
   \]

2. Calculate the moles of EDTA:
   \[
   \text{Moles of EDTA} = \text{Concentration} \times \text{Volume} = 0.02 \, \text{mol/dm}^3 \times 0.02170 \, \text{dm}^3 = 0.000434 \, \text{mol}
   \]

Since the reaction is 1:1, the moles of Cu²⁺ will also be 0.000434 mol.

3. Calculate the mass of copper using its molar mass (approximately 63.55 g/mol):
   \[
   \text{Mass of Cu} = \text{Moles of Cu} \times \text{Molar mass of Cu} = 0.000434 \, \text{mol} \times 63.55 \, \text{g/mol} = 0.0275797 \, \text{g}
   \]

4. Calculate the percent by mass of copper in compound X:
   \[
   \text{Percent by mass of Cu} = \left(\frac{\text{Mass of Cu}}{\text{Mass of X}}\right) \times 100 = \left(\frac{0.0275797}{0.1}\right) \times 100 = 27.5797\%
   \]
